task.title: Container runtime is reported unhealthy when `docker --version` takes longer than 2 seconds
task.body:
DCP considers the container runtime unhealthy when `docker --version` does not finish within 2 seconds (`dockerVersionCommandTimeout` in `internal/docker/cli_orchestrator.go`, unchanged on `main`). A container that is reconciled in that window goes to `RuntimeUnhealthy` (`controllers/container_controller.go`). @flojon analyzed this, with a deterministic reproduction, in microsoft/aspire#19570. I found no issue for it in this repository, so this adds the DCP side and data from another platform.

Environment: GitHub-hosted macOS Intel runner (4 vCPU), Docker engine in a Lima/QEMU VM, DCP 0.26.5 (Aspire 13.6.1).

**Observed (logs)**

- The DCP debug logs of 25 CI sessions contain 714 runs of `docker --version`: median 0.06 s, 95th percentile 0.64 s, 3 over 2 s (maximum 2.37 s).
- One session (passed) shows the sequence:

  ```
  15:47:56.318 Running Docker command ... docker --version
  15:47:56.951 Process started successfully                (0.63 s after the command was issued)
  15:47:58.321 Context expired, stopping process...        (the 2 s limit)
  15:47:59.752 NetworkReconciler: Container runtime is not healthy, retrying reconciliation later...
  ```
- In 3 of the 25 sessions DCP logged "Container runtime is not healthy", each time for the container network, which DCP retried (the tests passed). In none of them did a container reach `RuntimeUnhealthy`.
- In two earlier CI runs of one sample (no DCP log was captured), a container went from `Starting` to `RuntimeUnhealthy` after 0.2 s and 1.8 s, and everything that waited for it failed immediately.

**Assumed (not shown)**

- That those two failures were caused by this check. The signature matches, but I do not know which command failed.
- That the three slow calls belong to the three sessions where the runtime was reported unhealthy; I did not match them.

**Suggestion**

One of the options already listed in microsoft/aspire#19570, for example treating a `--version` timeout as "version unknown" instead of "not running", or retrying once before reporting `Running: false`.
